newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Commission presents beef label, passport plans.
newsitem.headline: Commission presents beef label, passport plans.

text.p: The European Commission presented proposals for cattle passports and beef labelling to farm ministers who asked their experts to study them, EU officials said on Tuesday.
The proposals, drawn up by the Commission on October 3, are part of efforts to try and restore consumer confidence after a public health scare over mad cow disease.
Some countries oppose the voluntary labelling plan because of the implications for single market law which bans the use of advertising claiming that one product is superior to another.
Other countries, such as Germany, want to see an even stronger labelling scheme in the interests of consumer safety.
Cattle passports, along with ear tags, would enable animals to be traced back to birth. Details would be kept on computer data bases.
